item.title: Pokémon Apps Are Coming Back Online After Extended Cybersecurity Outage

description.p: Sleep, HOME and Champions all went down yesterday.You may have read yesterday about the cybersecurity alert that hit sites and apps around the world after two vulnerabilities were found in the popular programming language, PHP. The Pokémon Company were one of the many teams hit by the outage, with Pokémon HOME, Sleep and Champions all going offline yesterday without an end time in sight. Well, fortunately, they have started to come back.As shared on the apps' official social media accounts, it seems that TPC is now on top of the issue and is in the process of restoring functionality. Champions was the first to come back online at around 3am BST this morning, followed by HOME a few hours later. Pokémon Sleep was a little later to join the party, but ended its maintenance around 10am BST.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: EA Outlines Future Development Plans As It Prepares To Cut Around 400 Jobs

description.p: Sports games remain top priority, unsurprisingly.Alongside the news Electronic Arts is shutting down BioWare and reports about it axing around 400 jobs across the entire company, EA executives have also revealed future development plans.According to an internal letter to staff, reviewed by Bloomberg, EA says it will continue investing in sports games (such as EA FC). Development on its online battle royale Apex Legends also remains a top priority, and it's supposedly still committed to its next Star Wars Jedi title as well as a new Marvel game starring Iron Man.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Award-Winning Indie Horror 'Mouthwashing' Finally Arrives On Switch This Month

description.p: Eye spy.Creepy space horror Mouthwashing became something of an indie sensation when it launched back in 2024. After racking up over 500,000 Steam sales, publisher Critical Reflex announced that a Switch version was in the works and now (a year on from that announcement), we finally have a release date.As revealed in yesterday's Xbox Showcase, Mouthwashing will launch on the Switch eShop on 29th October — yep, as in next week. It's already available to pre-order on the North American storefront, in fact, for $12.99. We've noticed that the store lists its release date as 10th October, but we're sure that's just a typo (we've reached out to Critical Reflex just to double-check).
